items.title: CoreWeave ARENA: Serverless inference and serverless RL
items.summary: See how prompt engineering helps an open-source model get close to a frontier model's accuracy on CoreWeave Serverless Inference, at a fraction of the cost. Compares an open source Text2SQL agent against the closed source Opus model by testing prompt engineering techniques on CoreWeave Serverless Inference. Using the same prompt and logging results to Weave, the presenter evaluates GLM 5.2 versus Opus 4.5 on accuracy and cost, moving from naive prompts through short examples, Chain of Thought, Self Consistency, Task Decomposition, and Skills. Opus performs much better than GLM 5.2 on the naive prompt, but Chain of Thought reduces the accuracy gap to about 3 points while Opus costs about 9 times more. Self Consistency improves accuracy but widens the gap again and costs 3 attempts, and GLM approaches Opus on most techniques except the naive prompt, achieving similar results at about a tenth of the price. items.title: Inside quantum-centric supercomputing
items.summary: One of the biggest misconceptions about quantum computing is that it will eventually replace classical computing, but that’s not the case. *All* quantum computing relies on classical computing, even just for loading data and reading outputs, and many of the most promising quantum use cases involve quantum processing units (QPUs) working alongside the CPUs and GPUs behind powerful classical supercomputers. However, figuring out how these different computing paradigms fit together is easier said than done. In this episode of The Coherence Times, we’re joined by IBM’s Seetharami Seelam and AMD’s Sanjay Chaurasia to explore the emerging world of quantum-centric supercomputing. Together, they discuss the similarities and differences between GPUs and QPUs, explain how quantum and classical systems work together, and offer a glimpse at the next generation of hybrid computing.
